text:
Maya: Heads-up — after the 535.xx driver push in prod this morning we're seeing a latency regression for medium-length requests (seq 128-512). P95 up ~18% and tail jitter increased. Kernel picks switched to the slower fallback path a lot more than before.

Dario: saw this on staging too. Kernel selection logs show repeated kernel-choice flips mid-inference when KV cache allocations happen. Could be allocator behavior.

Ash: any memory errors or OOMs in the logs?

Maya: no OOMs, but allocator free lists look more fragmented. `cuMemGetInfo()` free/total numbers are lower than expected between batches. Snapshot from one run: 
```
cuMemGetInfo: free=6.8GB total=40.0GB
batch start -> allocate KV cache chunk 1.2GB -> free=5.6GB
batch finish -> free returns to 6.4GB (not fully reclaimed)
next batch allocate 1.2GB fails to reuse contiguous chunk -> fallback kernel chosen
```

Priya: interesting — the fallback kernel is chosen when contiguous allocation fails because that kernel expects packed tensors. The autotuner logic treats allocation failures as a hard constraint.

Logan: do we know which part of the driver change could cause this? I remember release notes about changes to the CUDA memory allocator and deferred coalescing.

Dario: yes, release notes mention a change in the driver-side allocator that delays coalescing of freed blocks under certain fragmentation patterns. Combined with our rapid allocate/free of KV cache and batch buffers, that could create small holes.

Maya: repro recipe I ran on a 8xH100 test node: repeated small-batch chat requests with message-length variance triggers kernel choice flip within 10k steps. I pushed a flamegraph and allocation timeline to the perf channel.

Ash: can we tweak autoplay? Two options: 1) temporary rollback to driver 534.XX; 2) mitigation in runtime: prefer packing and defragmentation hints before kernel selection (try to coalesce via pre-warm alloc), or widen contiguous allocation threshold to allow fallback to still choose fast kernel and copy if necessary.

Priya: ops constraints: rollback needs maintenance window for many dedicated clusters and may affect other customers. Prefer runtime mitigations first. What's low-risk to ship as config toggle?

Dario: we can add a short pre-alloc step in the request pipeline: attempt to reserve and immediately release a contiguous KV cache slab sized to worst-case tail. If allocation fails, mark node as "fragmented" and switch to a more conservative batching policy (smaller batches, avoid large ephemeral allocations). This is purely runtime and reversible by config.

Maya: patch idea sketched: 
```
# prewarm slab (pseudo)
def prewarm_slab(node, slab_size):
    h = cudaMalloc(slab_size)
    if not h:
        node.meta['frag']=True
    else:
        cudaFree(h)
```
Then kernel selection consults node.meta['frag'] and biases heuristics to prefer kernels that tolerate non-contiguous buffers (with an extra memcpy cost) instead of failing into fallback.

Logan: also add a periodic defrag job that runs during low-util windows which allocates a large scratch buffer to encourage coalescing. Might nudge driver to coalesce. But test carefully.

Ash: we need telemetry: add metrics for `prewarm_slab_failures`, `kernel_fallback_count_by_seqlen`, and `kv_alloc_contig_failures`. That will help us decide whether runtime toggle suffices.

Maya: agreed. I'll open a canary config: enable prewarm on 10% of nodes in prod, collect metrics for 6 hours, and compare P95. If improvement >10% and no new regressions, widen rollout.

Dario: contingency plan if prewarm doesn't help: ops to schedule driver rollback for affected pools during next maintenance window. I'll draft rollback playbook — include driver pkg pinning, kernel-module compatibility checks, and canary validation steps (benchmarks and KV allocation traces).

Priya: +1. Also add a rollout kill-switch in config and a diagnostic endpoint that dumps current node.meta and recent allocation timeline.

OpsBot: deploy-bot: Canary prewarm toggle enabled on pool "dedicated-east-3" (10% nodes). Monitor: metric alert thresholds set: prewarm_failures > 5/min -> notify #eng-oncall.

Logan: one more thought — our autotuner currently treats allocation failures as deterministic block. Could we add a retry-with-defrag step before giving up on a fast kernel? Eg, try small sync-free defrag (release and reallocate ephemeral buffers) then re-evaluate kernel choice. Might avoid full copy path.

Maya: good idea. We'll implement both: prewarm probe + retry-defrag hook + telemetry. I'll own the runtime PR. Dario, please own the rollback playbook. Ash, Priya you own the canary validation and metric dashboards.

Dario: assigned. Drafting rollback doc now, will paste checklist here when ready.

Maya: thanks team. Will post PR link when ready and update this thread with initial canary metrics. :thumbsup:
